title: Secure Prefetching for Secure Cache Systems
problem: Secure cache systems like GhostMinion enforce on-commit prefetching to prevent speculative execution leakage, but this creates negative interactions with hardware prefetchers, causing redundant cache traffic, increased miss latency, and reduced prefetcher timeliness.
motivation: Secure cache systems must defend against transient execution attacks while maintaining high performance for practical deployment.
method: The authors analyze the interaction between state-of-the-art prefetchers and GhostMinion's invisible speculation-based secure cache system. They propose two microarchitectural solutions: (1) a redundant traffic filter that detects and eliminates duplicate cache updates during non-speculative operations, and (2) a secure prefetcher design that compensates for delayed prefetch request triggering at commit time to restore timeliness.
key_novelty: Combining redundant traffic filtering with commit-time prefetch compensation to recover prefetcher timeliness while maintaining security against speculative execution attacks.
contributions: First comprehensive analysis of interaction between hardware prefetchers and GhostMinion-style secure cache systems
Redundant cache traffic filter for non-speculative cache hierarchy updates
Secure prefetcher design ensuring prefetch request timeliness at commit without compromising security
Achieves 1.9-23% performance improvements with only 0.59 KB storage overhead per core

metrics.speedup: 1.9% single-core, 19.0% multi-core with filter; 6.3% single-core, 23.0% multi-core with secure prefetcher
